# Build output and disk cleanup

Rust `target` folders on active projects commonly grow to 60-115 GB each (incremental
caches, several profiles, test binaries, debug info), and every git worktree has its own.
Flutter `build` / `.dart_tool` and `node_modules` add several GB per checkout. A full disk
slows builds and makes them fail in confusing ways.

The audit lists the largest build-output folders. Deletion is the user's call - show the
list and the commands, don't run them.

## Safe to delete (regenerated by the next build)

| Folder | Command | Cost of deleting |
|---|---|---|
| Rust `target` | `cargo clean` in the repo (or delete the folder) | next build is a full build |
| Old Rust artifacts only | `cargo install cargo-sweep`, then `cargo sweep --time 14` (older than 14 days) or `cargo sweep --installed` (built by toolchains no longer installed) | keeps recent ones |
| Flutter | `flutter clean` | next build/pub get re-runs |
| `node_modules` | delete the folder, `npm ci` / `pnpm install` to restore | reinstall time |
| Worktrees you're done with | `git worktree remove <path>` (from the main repo) | removes the checkout and its build output |

Before deleting, make sure nothing is building or testing in that folder.

## Caches

- Cargo registry/git cache: recent cargo cleans unused downloads automatically; for more
  control, `cargo install cargo-cache` then `cargo cache --autoclean`.
- npm: `npm cache verify` (garbage-collects); pnpm: `pnpm store prune`.
- Pub: `dart pub cache clean` (removes everything; next `pub get` re-downloads).
- Gradle: delete `%USERPROFILE%\.gradle\caches` when no Gradle daemon is running
  (`gradlew --stop`).
- sccache: `sccache --show-stats`; the cache size is capped by `SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE`.

## Avoid a shared target folder across worktrees

Setting one `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` for several checkouts saves disk, but cargo decides
freshness by file timestamps and paths: builds from different worktrees overwrite each
other, and a build can reuse a binary built from *another* checkout. Prefer one target per
worktree and clean finished ones; use `sccache` if the goal is to share compiled
dependencies.

## WSL and container disks

WSL 2 distros (and Docker Desktop / Podman machines, which are WSL distros) store their
filesystem in an `ext4.vhdx` that grows but doesn't shrink on its own.

```powershell
wsl --list --verbose                        # what exists
wsl --shutdown                              # required before any of the below
# Newer WSL: make the disk sparse so it gives space back automatically
wsl --manage <distro> --set-sparse true
# Move a distro to another drive (newer WSL)
wsl --manage <distro> --move D:\wsl\<distro>
```

Inside containers, prune first: `podman system prune` / `docker system prune` (review what
it will remove - it deletes stopped containers and unused images). Undo for a move: move it
back the same way. Back up anything important inside a distro before moving it
(`wsl --export <distro> <file>.tar`).

Older WSL without `--manage`: compact with `Optimize-VHD -Path <vhdx> -Mode Full` (needs the
Hyper-V PowerShell module) or `diskpart` (`select vdisk file=...`, `compact vdisk`) after
`wsl --shutdown`.
